text:
maya: Observability alert — US-WEST serving cluster (pool-gpu-a) is under sustained max-batch pressure and we're missing latency SLOs for chat endpoints. p99 up ~2.1x, admission queue growing, prefills spiking.

maya: ```
model: redwood-7b-v1
region: us-west-2
active_gpus: 48/48
avg_queue_depth: 420
max_batch_pressure: 0.92
admission_reject_rate: 0.08
p99_latency_ms: 1290 (SLO 800)
prefill_rate_rps: 34 -> 210
cache_miss_rate: 0.27
```

liam: seeing the same in traces — hot hotspot on slot-3 and packing window is getting full. lots of prefills from demo-team jobs. :fire:

sanjay: can we throttle prefills at the ingress? looks like the demo SDK is firing larger prefill sizes after yesterday's client update.

eva: opsbot confirms autoscaler didn't add nodes — min capacity is reached and policy needs both util and headroom signals, which we're not emitting.

tom: quick question — would lowering max_batch for redwood-7b-v1 on this pool reduce pack pressure? it might increase per-token latency a bit but reduce queuing.

rachel: :eyes: Another short-term option: fallback some traffic to q4-quantized model for non-SLA tenants.

liam: list of immediate mitigations I recommend:
1) temporarily rate-limit demo-team prefill endpoints.
2) lower max_batch from 128 -> 64 on pool-gpu-a for redwood-7b-v1.
3) enable single-request fast-path for requests with small prompt lengths to avoid packing overhead.

maya: I'll open an emergency rollout. @deploy-bot can we get an admission-controller patch that short-circuits admission for requests with high prefill-token counts if kv-cache-miss-rate > 0.2?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: queued rollout request received for admission-controller v1.23-rc. Running preflight checks. Canary pods: 3/3 available.

sanjay: also need a quick trace to map kv-cache coldstarts to client ids. I'll run a targeted eval and post counts in 10m.

eva: if traffic shaping + rollout doesn't stabilize within 20m, we should request burst capacity from capacity team — autoscaler won't help because GPUs are saturated. @liam can you file?

liam: filed INF-3345: request +8 GPUs in us-west for 2 hours to reduce admission pressure. ETA: ~18m. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3345

maya: applied demo-team rate-limit and lowered max_batch on pool-gpu-a. Initial telemetry: queue depth -> 210, p99 down to 920ms and trending downward. still above SLO but improved.

tom: next engineering action: change admission scoring to penalize prefill-heavy requests and bias for small-reqs. I'll sketch RFC and add opt-in flag for canary pools.

rachel: long-term: hook autoscaler to kv-cache-miss-rate and prefill-rate as a signal (headroom metric) so we autoscale earlier for coldstart-heavy workloads.

liam: note on cost tradeoff — temporary +8 GPUs for 2h is cheaper than prolonged SLO misses for paid customers, but we should log chargeback.

eva: rough cost calc sent to finance: 8 gpus * $3/hr * 2 hr = ~$48 raw (network/storage overhead not included).

maya: thanks all, monitoring. will update when p99 < 850ms or if rollback needed. :thumbsup:

liam: quick logs snippet showing admission queue shrink:```
[2023-11-15T17:02:12Z] admission_queue_depth=620
[2023-11-15T17:12:12Z] admission_queue_depth=410
[2023-11-15T17:22:12Z] admission_queue_depth=210
```

sanjay: posted kv-cache coldstart breakdown in the observability thread — demo-team accounts are >60% of coldstarts.

maya: closing the immediate incident in 30m unless we regress. good debug notes for postmortem.

rachel: +1 on postmortem — include config changes, rollout ids, and cost addendum.

opsbot: incident-ticket #INC-2023-211 created and linked to INF-3345.

maya: end of thread update: admission-controller patch rolled to canary and then prod; queue stabilized. follow-up action items assigned in the postmortem doc.
